15039e5821.why: Old two-answer problem fixed: the lure is now about the Sun itself ('burning hotter, then cooler') and cannot be read as the heat a place receives. It is false: total solar irradiance varies about 0.1 percent over the 11-year cycle, and the yearly swing in sunlight reaching Earth is orbital, not solar. Key true (NASA: 'Earth's tilted axis causes the seasons'); distance and the Moon truly wrong. Choices parallel in length, all live, no stem word picked up by the key. Core 6th-grade fact; no T1 unit asks the cause of the seasons. Context true (147.1 to 152.1 million km).

b9696464d8.why: Old nudge fixed: the stem no longer says the axis is 'carried along', and no longer calls it tilted, so 'It stands straight up in spring and autumn' stays live. No stem word echoed by the key ('year-long' and 'through the year' are shared with a lure too). Key true: NASA, 'its tilted axis always points in the same direction'; Wikipedia Axial parallelism, the only change is precession over about 26,000 years, with no yearly rocking. All three lures are real misconceptions (M3) and truly wrong. 6th-grade seasons model content.

dfcf720c68.why: Old tell fixed: the slant clause is gone and the key 'Its light is spread over a wider area' shares no word with the stem. The low-Sun picture still points at angle, but turning a low Sun into a spread beam is the grade's simple why, and the distance lure (M1, sourced) stays strongly live. Key true (NASA: the hemisphere tilted away gets 'its rays from more of an angle'; Wikipedia: rays 'spread over a larger area'). Lures false: Earth is nearer the Sun in December, the Sun's output barely changes, the length of day varies by about a millisecond. The perihelion hint for c957dcd792 is gone from the context. Not the T1 shadow-length fact.

467cf2d824.why: Old elimination tell fixed: one date, so the two hemisphere choices are no longer ruled out by the stem, and the dead 'nights longer everywhere' lure is replaced by 'equal only along the equator', which tempts because the equator has about 12 hours all year. The stem's 'Spring begins in the Northern Hemisphere' makes the northern lure live, not the key. Key true and properly hedged: Grokipedia Equinox, day and night are 'only approximately equal', and both poles have 'continuous daylight for approximately four days around each equinox'; March equinox March 19-21. Refraction lengthens the day by minutes everywhere, so no hemisphere choice is defensible over 'about equal'. The hedge words in the key are needed for truth and do not make it stand out. 6th-grade content.

8065db90ab.why: New question, a different fact from the dropped repeat. Key true: Grokipedia Seasonal_lag, 'The primary cause is the high specific heat capacity of water', peak warmth about four to six weeks after the June solstice; Wikipedia, the lag is 'largely caused by the presence of large amounts of water'; EarthSky, the Sun has to 'warm the oceans' first, 'the lag of the seasons'. Lures false: aphelion is early July, the Sun's output does not peak in July, days shorten after the June solstice. Stem names the noon Sun's height, so it rules out no lure and does not give away 591a09856e. 'Far north of the equator' rightly keeps the girl out of the tropics. RULING on the T1 sea-breeze question (weather-and-climate-basics, 'The Sun warms the land faster than the sea'): a different fact, not a repeat. The T1 item keys a daily wind from land and sea heating at different rates side by side; this keys the seasonal lag, a delay over the year in when the hottest weeks come. The key states no land-sea comparison and no wind, and the student must carry the slow-warming water to a new case, which is the T2 'basic fact and its simple why'. A player who knows the T1 fact is helped, as later grades should build on earlier ones. Non-blocking polish: the context's 'Water soaks up heat slowly' is loose (water absorbs sunlight readily; its temperature rises slowly), and 'Water warms up slowly' would be exact.
